prompt: A developer's sustainability consultant needs to know which organization will review the project's LEED certification documentation and which one administers the LEED Green Associate exam the consultant plans to take. Which organization handles both?

U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC), the nonprofit that writes and updates the rating systems
ASHRAE, the society whose referenced standards set the baseline for many LEED requirements
The local building department, which verifies LEED compliance during its final code inspection

explanation: LEED separates standard-setting from verification. USGBC, a nonprofit, develops the rating systems, while GBCI independently reviews certification applications and administers LEED professional credential exams such as the Green Associate. That separation is what makes LEED a third-party verified program.

distractorExplanations.b: USGBC develops LEED and offers education, but it does not review project applications or run the credential exams; that independent role sits with GBCI.
distractorExplanations.c: ASHRAE publishes standards such as 90.1 and 62.1 that LEED references, but it has no role in reviewing LEED projects or testing LEED professionals.
distractorExplanations.d: Code officials enforce the building code, not LEED; LEED is a voluntary program whose credits are verified by GBCI reviewers rather than at a code inspection.

The environmental attributes of renewable generation fed into the grid elsewhere
A rebate from its utility that lowers the price per kilowatt-hour on its bill
Offsets for the refrigerant emissions released by its building cooling systems

explanation: A REC represents the environmental attributes of one megawatt-hour of renewable electricity delivered to the grid. Buying RECs lets the company claim that renewable generation; the electrons it uses still come from the local grid mix, because grid power cannot be physically traced to a single generator.

distractorExplanations.a: Grid electricity cannot be routed from one generator to one meter; the REC is a separate certificate that carries the renewable claim.
distractorExplanations.c: RECs are purchased from a market or supplier and do not change the utility tariff; the company still pays its normal electricity rate.
distractorExplanations.d: RECs address electricity-related emissions; refrigerant leaks are a separate direct emission source handled through refrigerant management.

prompt: An owner asks why the team recommends investing in efficiency measures before sizing a rooftop solar array. What is the strongest reason?

Utilities require a completed efficiency audit before approving any solar interconnection
Lower energy demand means a smaller array can cover a larger share of the building's use
Efficiency measures qualify for green power credits that solar arrays cannot earn

explanation: Efficiency is usually the cheapest kilowatt-hour. distractorExplanations.b: Interconnection rules vary by utility and generally address electrical safety, not an efficiency audit; this is not the reason for the sequence.
distractorExplanations.d: Efficiency does not generate green power credits; green power and RECs relate to renewable generation, not to reduced consumption.

prompt: A team is comparing replacement refrigerants for a chiller. One option has zero ozone depletion potential (ODP) but a very high global warming potential (GWP). How should the team assess it?

It harms both the ozone layer and the climate, because ODP and GWP rise and fall together
It is climate neutral, because a refrigerant with zero ODP has no warming effect if released
It is ideal for decarbonization, because GWP applies only to combustion gases such as CO2

distractorExplanations.c: Zero ODP says nothing about heat-trapping; a high-GWP refrigerant released to the air warms the climate far more than the same mass of CO2.

prompt: A specifier is reviewing paints, adhesives, and sealants for an interior fit-out. Why do volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in these products matter?

They make the products harder to recycle at the end of their service life

prompt: Drywall sanding is under way on a project while the permanent air handlers must run to condition the space. Which construction practice best protects indoor air quality?

Sealing return openings and installing temporary filtration on the air handlers
Scheduling the building flush-out before drywall finishing begins
Storing drywall and insulation outdoors, uncovered, so dust stays outside the building

prompt: A facility manager is comparing HVAC filters labeled with different MERV ratings. What does a higher MERV rating indicate?

Greater ability to remove gaseous VOCs and odors from the recirculated air
Longer service life before the filter needs to be replaced in the air handler
Higher efficiency at capturing smaller airborne particles from the airstream

explanation: MERV (Minimum Efficiency Reporting Value), determined under ASHRAE Standard 52.2, rates how well a filter captures particles across size ranges. distractorExplanations.c: MERV is a capture-efficiency rating, not a service-life rating; replacement intervals depend on dust loading and pressure drop.
